newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr remains firm but upside test fails in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr remains firm but upside test fails in Tokyo.

text.p: 0312 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar remained firm against the yen by midday Tokyo but failed to retest 119 yen amid lingering fears over possible comments by Japanese monetary officials to talk down the dollar, dealers said.
Mark's underlying weakness against the yen indirectly limited the dollar's advance against the yen, while the dollar maintained gains versus the mark from Friday's strong rally.

"The dollar is strong based on differences in strength in economy (between United States and Japan)," a city bank dealer said, adding that buying interest on dips will support the greenback near 118.30 yen for now.
But dealers said buying energy somewhat dimmed as the dollar approached 119 yen due to growing concerns about possible verbal intervention by Japanese officials.

"I don't think there will be a concrete action (to sell dollars) by authorities unless the dollar rises to around 125 yen, but wariness over possible intervention becomes intact when the dollar nears 119 yen," a bank dealer said.

Japanese institutional investors were said to be keen to buy dollars in early trade, possibly in connection with their fresh investments, but profit-taking by interbank dealers and light exporter sales halted the dollar's rise just below 119 yen.

The dollar maintained its bullish tone against the mark by midday after surging in New York on Friday due to fresh evidence of strength in the U.S. economy, such as stronger-than-expected U.S. non-farm payrolls data, which fuelled expectations of higher interest rates.
The dollar ended at 118.35/45 yen and 1.8620/30 marks after rising as high as 1.8665 marks in New York on Friday.

U.S. non-farm payrolls increased 316,000 in July, pushing unemployment rate down to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June. Economists had forecast, on average, an increase of 193,000 in July non-farm payrolls.
In addition, uncertainty about the planned single European currency will keep weighing on the mark, dealers said.

They added that mark short-covering interest for yen, which was detected earlier in the morning after a sharp drop on Friday, has somewhat lost steam by midday. The German unit stood near 63.63/66 yen at 0340 GMT, compared with 63.67 yen in early Tokyo trade.
The city bank dealer said that he was watching moves in Japanese stocks, and that weaker Tokyo stocks could provide support to the dollar against the yen.
The Tokyo stock market's key index slid below the key 19,500 threshold in early afternoon trade on Monday for the first time since July 9.
